recipes.name: Pork Carnitas
ingredients_raw: 4 pounds pork shoulder, cut into several large pieces

steps.text: Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven over high heat. Season pork shoulder pieces with salt, then arrange in the Dutch oven. Cook until browned on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Stir in onion, garlic, lime juice, chili powder, oregano, and cumin. Pour in chicken broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until pork is very tender, about 2 1/2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Transfer pork shoulder to a large baking sheet; reserve cooking liquid. Drizzle a small amount of cooking liquid over pork pieces and lightly season with salt.
Bake pork in the preheated oven until browned, about 30 minutes. Drizzle more cooking liquid every 10 minutes; use two forks to shred pork as it browns.

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Carnitas
raw_recipe.description: Carnitas, or Mexican pulled pork, is made by slow cooking pork until perfectly tender and juicy, then roasting the shredded pork for deliciously crisp edges.

video.description: Pork Carnitas - yes please! In this video, you'll see how to make homemade pork carnitas which are the perfect filling for tacos, nachos, and tostadas. Pork shoulder is seared and browned and simmered in a garlic lime broth. Then off to the oven for more browning, shredding, and flavoring.

review.reviewBody:
Hi all, Keep in mind, the objective of the final step is to get slightly crispy outside with a moist, tender inside. The recipe says a "clove" of garlic ... I meant a bulb, but of course, garlic to taste, and for that matter, salt. Remember to adjust your salt and spices to the size of the roast, but broth doesn't need the same levels of increases. If you're not a salty person, salt the roast as you normally would. If you feel like you're over-salting, then you probably are. Also, make sure you're using Kosher style salt. If reg. salt, use less. The level of fat on your roast also plays a role - more fat, less salt. Written a long time ago -- I don't use cans of broth, just the sealed boxes -- about 1 will do. I have also used pork loin, and it tends to dry out-- try to buy one with more fat than you normally would. Shoulder/butt is much better.

I often put the dutch oven in the oven at about 300-325 degrees, depending on how fast you need it to cook. I have a summer version where I marinate the pork pieces in lime, garlic, olive oil, adobo chili sauce, cilantro, and onion. I then grill outdoors to get the browned edges, and then set up a disposable aluminum pan covered with foil to do the braising in broth. I keep it on the grill on very low heat until tender. Then move the pieces indoors to finish with the same steps as the winter version. 

Some great ideas here - crock pot/ coke/beer. It's not an exact science. It's just a cooking technique.

I cubed the pork and browned it in 2 tablespoons of oil, in a pressure cooker. I substituted cilantro for oregano. I increased garlic 3 cloves. Omitted chili powder. Held off on salt. Increased cumin to 1 tbs and added 2 tsp coriander. I added strips of 2 poblano, 1 jalapeno and 1 serreano peppers. I substituted 2 chicken boullion cubes for 4 cans and 1 bottle 16.9 oz drinking water for water. I placed all ingredients in an electric pressure cooker, on high, for 90 minutes. After a normal release, I adjusted the salt and spread refried beans on a large flour tortilla with a scoop of this Pork Carnitas, Herdez hot salsa and Monterey jack cheese for one of the best burritos I've ever tasted.

Great instructional. I eyeballed my measurements. I used about 1/4 cup of dried homegrown chili powder. A mix of (Calabrian sweet, Palermo longs, pimente d'esplette), a couple of tablespoons of smoked paprika, toasted and ground cumin, homegrown music garlic (extremely pungent and aromatic Italian heirloom)I cut up my meat into large chunks (a 7 pound boneless butt) and marinated it overnight in garlic, chilis, oregano, salt and tellicherry pepper - poured a couple cups of pineapple juice over and massaged it all. This morning I browned the meat and placed it in my crock pot. I cooked up a little bit to test seasoning - adjusted with 2 tablespoons of chicken stock paste - more pineapple juice. Cooking on high in crock pot. Will finish in the oven to crisp. I plan to freeze what we don't eat tonight. I will place portions in sealed container to thaw and crisp in a pan or oven. I chose to not add onions yet - I plan to add pickled onions to our tacos. I thought the flavors are excellent without onion. Go figure! ;-)

I made this as directed with the exception of the pork as I had lefover pork roast that was already shredded for pulled pork. I halved the recipe based upon the amount of port I had available. I did add one can of mild diced green chilis and a couple tablespoons of chopped jalapeno. Since I used pork that was already cooked, I made the sauce and brought it to a boil and tasted to ensure the flavor was there before adding the pork. I simmered on low heat for 45 minutes before transferring to the sheet pan. I finished the recipe as printed. This was very tasty and will be making again.

I've made this recipe alot it is better than any restaurant carnitas I've tried. That being said use your head with the salt 3 Tbsp is wayyyy too much I use 1 Tbsp and also I increase the oven time by approximately 15 minutes . The end product is slightly crispy on the outside and buttery on the inside.....

I cooked this in my Instant Pot using the ingredients listed. When it was done, I put a little caramelization to the pork and onions using my crisping lid. Then I fried two tortillas with cheese between them (like quesadillas). We filled the cheese filled tortillas with the carnitas and added fresh chopped cilantro, avocado, and tomato. Topped with a sauce of sour cream, mayonnaise, lime juice, sugar, cumin, and chipotle hot sauce. We rolled or folded them and used a lot of napkins. DELICIOUS!!

Excelled recipe. Meat is fork-tender even without a Dutch oven as long as the chunks are (almost completely) covered by the liquid. I seasoned with salt to my preference and adjusted at the end when it went in the oven. I also recommending adding more lime in the broth or squeezing additional sauce when it goes in the oven.

I used a 4# pork loin roast and cut off the fat. Cut into 2" pieces and sauteed in a large skillet until browned, then added the rest of the ingredients, then added the broth. Simmered for 2 hours, then shredded in the pot. I didn't crisp in the oven & I didn't add any salt, we are watching our salt intake, so I have to watch that. Excellent recipe and served with refried beans, flour tortillas, salsa, sour cream, fresh diced tomatoes and it was wonderful!
I cooked my pork in a slow cooker over night. The flavor was better than I imagined. I did add jalapeño's for a little extra kick and extra garlic.

This is an excellent recipe. Normally I make and review recipes exactly as written but I did change a couple of spices based on other reviews. I omitted the cinnamon and Chinese 5 spice, and added 2 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp cumin and 1 tsp oregano as per Chef John's suggestion. I also added 1 yellow onion chunked just because we love onion. It was flavored perfectly and had the richness we've been searching for that has been missing in other recipes. I did a chunky shred before broiling and it was easy to make the tacos. Served with pico de gallo, lime and sour cream, this is a fabulous recipe and will be my go-to from now on. Bravo Chef John!

I made it using the pressure cooker. First browned meat as specified...when I added the broth, I started the pressure cooking. All done in 35 minutes. Absolutely delicious. I salted to my taste so I had no problem.
next time ill only add have to salt, it was a little over salty but tasted amazing

We've made this recipe several times since we found it a few years ago. It freezes well, and sometimes I have brought the frozen carnitas to heat up for an easy first meal on a road trip or camping. We use kosher salt and less of it than the recipe asks for. We often add higher amounts of the seasonings when we cook it and sometimes add some orange juice or coca-cola. Such a terrific recipe to use and make it your own. So yummy! Definitely a keeper.
Big batch recipe that hits all the marks for flavor, texture, and freezes well. I make it regularly now and keep good amounts on hand.
Yummy!
Yes indeed!

I'm not one to change a recipe and then leave a review but for this recipe I reduced salt. Against my better judgement I added 1.5 tablespoons of salt instead of 3 tablespoons as written and the finished product is more salty than I'd like. Generally I add 3/4 of a teaspoon of salt per pound of meat which for many is too salty. If I'd followed the recipe as written my pork would be inedible.
Good flavor but I’d probably use thx crock pot next time.
I made no changes. My husband says they are the best carnitas he has ever had, and he always orders carnitas when we eat Mexican food out,

I have made this dozens of times and my son, who is food bougie, says I make it better than any Mexican restaurant... and I live in the Central Valley. I don't use quite as much salt and only enough broth to cover the meat, but everything else is a chef's kiss of deliciousness!
